title: Midnight Breach at Cipher Labs
story: Maya, a senior cybersecurity analyst at Cipher Labs, discovered that the encrypted backup of her zero‑day exploit had been wiped from the company server at 02:15 AM UTC. The server logs recorded a successful SSH login from the internal IP 10.0.0.45 at exactly that moment. Four people had access to that credential: Leo, the senior developer; Nina, the IT administrator; Omar, a freelance penetration tester hired for the week; and Priya, the project manager who also handled key‑management. Leo swears he was debugging code in the lounge until 03:00 AM local time. Nina says she was reviewing firewall rules from home and never left her desk. Omar claims he was on a scheduled video call with a client in Tokyo, which started at 10:15 PM his local time (01:15 AM UTC) and ended at 01:45 AM UTC. Priya insists she was still on that same call when the breach occurred, noting the call’s timestamp shows she was active until 02:00 AM UTC. After the incident, a USB flash drive bearing Priya’s personal encryption key was found in the server room trash bin, and the drive’s metadata shows it was last used at 02:10 AM UTC.
crimeScene: Cipher Labs server room, Silicon Valley
forensicClue: USB flash drive with Priya’s encryption key found in trash, last used at 02:10 AM UTC
question: Who erased Maya’s encrypted backup and how was the culprit identified?
options: Option A (Leo – He was debugging code in the lounge)
Option B (Nina – She was reviewing firewall rules from home)
Option C (Priya – Her USB key was found in the trash and the timeline doesn’t fit her alibi)
Option D (Omar – He was on a video call that ended before the breach)
deductionExplanation: 1. The server log shows a login at 02:15 AM UTC from IP 10.0.0.45. Only the four suspects have credentials for that IP. 2. Omar’s call ended at 01:45 AM UTC, so he could not have logged in at 02:15 AM. 3. Nina was at home and has no record of accessing the server at that hour. 4. Leo was in the lounge until 03:00 AM, but the lounge is on a separate VLAN and cannot reach the internal IP 10.0.0.45. 5. Priya claimed she was still on the call until 02:00 AM UTC, but the call log ends at 02:00 AM, leaving a 15‑minute gap before the breach. 6. The decisive forensic clue is the USB flash drive with Priya’s personal encryption key, found in the server‑room trash and last used at 02:10 AM UTC – just five minutes before the login. The only person who could have used that key at that time is Priya, making her the indisputable culprit.
